Hi Alice —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call highlights:
- FintechCo is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for inference across payments fraud and risk models.
- Primary constraints: predictable unit cost, auditability (KMS + audit logs), and support SLAs.

Action items / asks for pricing qualification:
1) Monthly token volumes by workload (approximate ranges ok): generation tokens vs embeddings tokens.
2) Target unit economics / budget goal (e.g., $X per 1M tokens or monthly committed spend).
3) Environment footprint: how many environments (prod / staging / dev / DR) you expect to run?
4) Support preference: Standard vs Priority (Priority includes 24/7 on-call + faster TTR).

Attached is our draft pricing worksheet (redwood_private_pricing_v2.pdf) — it outlines two commercial models we typically use for Private: 1) capacity-based license (monthly seat + GPU capacity commit) and 2) license + usage overage (lower commit, higher per-token).

If you can send token ranges and preferred support tier, I’ll have Marissa (account) and Dev (SE) produce a tailored quote and environment sizing.

Target next step: internal sizing call with your infra team later this week — are you available Thurs/Fri PST?

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. See high-level answers below (we pulled these from our telemetry and internal forecasts; attaching the detailed breakout).

- Monthly token volumes (30-day avg across prod workloads):
  - Fraud detection / real-time scoring (generation + context): ~200M tokens/month
  - Batch risk scoring (embeddings + rerank): ~50M tokens/month
  - Feature enrichment / telemetry parsing: ~25M tokens/month
  => Total approx: 275M tokens/month (we're forecasting up to 400M in peak months over the next 12 months)

- Target unit economics / budget:
  - We're aiming for ~$300 - $400 per 1M tokens (this is our internal target to replace existing infra costs).

- Environments:
  - Prod: 2 clusters (primary + hot-standby)
  - Staging: 1 cluster
  - Dev: shared dev environment (non-prod)
  - DR: optional, would prefer warm-standby if cost-effective

- Preferred support: Priority (we require faster TTR and a named technical contact during onboarding)

Attaching our token breakout sheet: fintechco_token_usage_estimate.xlsx

Thanks Alice — this is exactly what we needed. Quick notes based on your numbers and target $/1M: 

1) Licensing model recommendation (based on 275M baseline, up to 400M peak):
   - Option A (Capacity license): monthly GPU capacity commit (sized for steady-state ~300–350M tokens) + fixed monthly license fee. This gives the most predictable per-token cost and preferred for Priority support customers.
   - Option B (Lower commit + usage): smaller commit, lower monthly license, with per-token overage priced at X per 1M tokens. This provides flexibility for high growth but higher unit cost at higher volumes.

2) Ballpark unit economics we can achieve on a Capacity license (illustrative):
   - $220–$320 per 1M tokens with a 12-month commit (depends on model family, quantization, and batching profile).
   - For your $300–$400 target, Capacity license with some quantization/optimization should comfortably fit; Option B would land towards the top end of your range on peak months.

3) Environment count implications:
   - Prod (2 clusters): we recommend dedicated capacity for primary cluster and smaller reserved capacity for standby to meet SLA and failover.
   - Staging/dev: can be consolidated on shared lower-capacity pools (saves cost).

4) Next steps we suggest:
   - SE sizing call (Dev) Friday 8am PST — confirm and we’ll send calendar invite.
   - I'll follow up with a preliminary commercial template (monthly fees, commit levels, and overage rates) and a sample SOW/SLAs for Priority support.

Dev: can you prepare a quick sizing recommendation (GPU count, estimated sustained tokens/sec) for the Friday call?

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
